summary.text: Marlon Amprey is a Democratic member of the Maryland House of Delegates from District 40 who has served since January 13, 2021, and he is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
An attorney and former teacher, he serves on the Economic Matters Committee, where he chairs the Housing and Real Property Subcommittee.

paragraphs.text: Marlon Amprey was born in Baltimore on January 24, 1987, and earned a B.A. from the University of Maryland, College Park, in 2009 and a master's in education from George Mason University in 2011, according to his General Assembly biography.
He taught elementary school as a Teach For America corps member in Washington, D.C., from 2009 to 2011 and was a sixth-grade lead teacher at The SEED School of Maryland from 2011 to 2013.

He earned a J.D. from the University of Pennsylvania Law School in 2016 and has worked as an associate at Baltimore and Washington law firms since then, most recently at Rosenberg Martin Greenberg, LLP.

Ballotpedia reports that the Baltimore City Democratic State Central Committee nominated Amprey to the House on December 29, 2020; his official biography lists him as a member since January 13, 2021 and first elected in November 2022.
He served on the Environment and Transportation Committee from 2021 to 2023, has been on the Economic Matters Committee since 2023, and was Deputy Majority Whip from 2023 to 2026.
He is treasurer of the Legislative Black Caucus of Maryland, and Ballotpedia reports that he advanced from the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary.
